public.title: What does add(2, 3) give back?
public.prompt: add prints the sum. What value does the caller get from add(2, 3)?
options: Nothing, because add throws an error

hints.text: add only calls console.log. Nothing in it can throw here.
A function hands a value back only through a return statement. Look for one in add.

explanations.workedExample: console.log prints 5 but returns undefined. A function with no return statement hands undefined back to its caller.
explanations.practice: Write double(n) so it returns n * 2. The caller can then store the result.

segments.text: Here is add. It takes two numbers and prints their sum. Before we run it, predict the value that add(2, 3) gives back.
Run it. The sum prints in the console. Now think about what the caller actually receives from add.
Add a return statement. Now the caller receives 5, and the function stops at that line.
Next, the lab asks you to write a function that returns a value. Run your code and check the sample tests.

lab.instructions: Write double(n) so it returns n times 2. The program reads one number from stdin, passes it to double and prints the result.
